summary: Yuishin Ito (1931–2023) worked in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Bukkyo University and Doshisha University. He taught at Bukkyo University (lecturer from 1961, emeritus 1974–1997) and headed Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College (1997) and Kyoto Bunkyo Gakuen (~1999).

Yujiro Motora (1858–1912) was a scholar of philosophy and other fields who studied at Johns Hopkins University in 1885. He held posts at Tokyo University of Education (~1888–1900) and the University of Tokyo (~1888–1912).

Yujun Endo (1939–2017) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He taught at Taisho University as an associate professor (attested 1991) and later professor emeritus (attested 2014), and served as an advisor at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).
Yuka Otani is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a part-time lecturer at both Ryukoku University and Hanazono University (attested 2015).

Yukari Kimura specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her doctorate under Kenyu Mitomo and is attested in 2026 as affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and as a part-time lecturer at Rissho University.

Yukei Matsunaga (1929–2023) specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Koyasan, Tohoku, and Kyushu universities. He served as Director at Koyasan University (1983) and held a post at Shuchiin University (~1999–2004).

Yuki Sasaki works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, Sasaki has served as a part-time lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Yuki Takatsukasa is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015) and later served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2017).

Yukihiko Asayama worked in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. Asayama served as a professor at Hokkaido University of Education (attested 1986) and as a Ministry of Education overseas researcher at South China Normal University (attested 1991).
Yukihiko Matsumura specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. Matsumura studied at Tohoku University (attested 2015) and later served there as a specialist researcher (attested 2026).

Yukihiro Okada specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Michael Hahn. He served at Kobe Women's University Seto Junior College (emeritus attested 2015) and Minobusan University (advisor attested 2026).

Yukihisa Yamao (1935–2021) specialized in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Ritsumeikan University (~1954–1962) and subsequently served on the faculty there from around 1967 to 2001.

Yukio Hattori (1932–2007) was a Japanology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Nagoya University from around 1951 to 1957. He held a post at Japan Women's University from around 1971 to 1975.

Yukio Kotani (born 1931) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Hanjiro Tominaga. He served at Rissho University (~1972–2002), where he became an emeritus professor of comparative literature.

Yukio Sakamoto (1899–1973) studied at the University of Tokyo under Taiken Kimura and Daito Shimaji, and earned a doctorate from Tohoku University. He was a professor at Toyo University (~1930–1944) and later professor (1948) and president (1968) of Rissho University.

Yukio Takeda (1934–2021) was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1954–1963). He held faculty posts at Hokkaido University, Nagoya City University, the University of Tokyo (~1977–1995), and Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University (~2001–2006).

Yukio Yamanaka is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied as a graduate student at Kyoto University (attested 1996). Yamanaka was a DFG Research Fellow at the University of Göttingen (attested 2015).

Yuko Kamishima (b. 1971) studied at Indiana University Bloomington, Cambridge, and the University of Tokyo. Active in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, she held posts at Waseda University (2006–2016) and Ritsumeikan University (professor in 2016).
Yuko Matsuda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin Women's Junior College and later held an appointment at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2001).

Yuko Yokochi is an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara and Katsuhiko Kamimura, and earned a PhD from the University of Groningen under Hans T. Bakker. She served as associate professor at Kyoto University (attested 2002–2021).
